import React from "react"; import { Container, Typography, Box, Paper, Button, Table, TableBody, TableCell, TableContainer, TableHead, TableRow, } from "@mui/material"; import { useNavigate } from "react-router-dom"; import { ArrowBack, Calculate } from "@mui/icons-material"; import Navigation from "../../components/Navigation"; const DeductiblesPage: React.FC = () => { const navigate = useNavigate(); const exampleScenarios = [ { scenario: "Low Deductible Plan", deductible: "₹10,000", premium: "₹15,000/year", hospital: "₹1,00,000", youPay: "₹10,000 + ₹18,000", insurance: "₹72,000", total: "₹28,000", }, { scenario: "High Deductible Plan", deductible: "₹50,000", premium: "₹8,000/year", hospital: "₹1,00,000", youPay: "₹50,000 + ₹10,000", insurance: "₹40,000", total: "₹60,000", }, ]; return ( <> Understanding Deductibles Learn how deductibles work and how they impact your premium and out-of-pocket expenses. What is a Deductible? A deductible is the amount you must pay out-of-pocket for covered healthcare services before your insurance plan starts to pay. For example, if your deductible is ₹25,000, you pay the first ₹25,000 of covered services yourself. After that, you typically pay only a co-payment or co-insurance, and your insurer pays the rest. How Deductibles Work
  • You pay the deductible: When you receive healthcare services, you pay the full cost until you reach your deductible amount.
  • Cost sharing begins: After meeting your deductible, you and your insurance share costs through co-payments or co-insurance.
  • Out-of-pocket maximum: Once you reach this limit, insurance pays 100% of covered services for the rest of the year.
  • Annual reset: Deductibles reset each policy year, usually on January 1st or your policy renewal date.
    • Deductible vs. Premium Trade-off Generally, plans with higher deductibles have lower monthly premiums, while plans with lower deductibles have higher premiums. Here's a comparison: Aspect Low Deductible High Deductible Monthly Premium Higher Lower Out-of-pocket before coverage Lower Higher Best for Frequent healthcare users Healthy individuals Example ₹5,000 - ₹15,000 ₹25,000 - ₹50,000
    Real-World Example Let's say you need a hospital treatment costing ₹1,00,000. Here's how different deductible plans would work: Plan Type Deductible Annual Premium Hospital Bill You Pay Insurance Pays {exampleScenarios.map((row, index) => ( {row.scenario} {row.deductible} {row.premium} {row.hospital} {row.youPay} {row.insurance} ))}
    *Assuming 20% co-insurance after deductible is met 💡 Choosing the Right Deductible
  • Choose a low deductible if: You expect to use healthcare services frequently, have ongoing medical conditions, or prefer predictable costs.
  • Choose a high deductible if: You're generally healthy, can afford emergency expenses, and want to save on monthly premiums.
  • Consider your emergency fund: Can you afford to pay the full deductible if needed? Ensure you have savings to cover it.
    • 🎯 Find Your Perfect Balance Our AI tool analyzes your health profile, budget, and risk tolerance to recommend plans with the optimal premium-deductible balance.     ); }; export default DeductiblesPage;
